environment: Windows, local disposable PostgreSQL 16.2, ordinary NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS role, production HTTP runtime

fixture.contains: Synthetic biographies and events; no production data

mutation: One atomic batch: parent addition, new ancestor, event, source, union and additional relationship
method: tests/integration/postgres-live-changes.ts. archive.read and archive.write throw during HTTP delta/undo. Counts JSON serialization of .all() result sets only, excluding .get(), wire protocol overhead and INSERT/UPDATE commands. Each measurement uses a new disposable database. These are individual local measurements, not throughput/load benchmarks or a measured speedup against the previous implementation.

fragmentProtocol.smallScope: 1 authorized person does not activate a fragment despite 1001 global people
fragmentProtocol.limitations: One local synthetic PostgreSQL 16.2 run, not a concurrent throughput benchmark. Full snapshots/overviews are forbidden by throwing spies during active-fragment requests.

verified: Full archive hydration and replacement cannot run during current-revision minimal delta writes
Untouched person JSON and photo records are preserved
Inverse history reconstructs all records and fields
Stale conflicting fields return 409; cycles and foreign catalog IDs roll back
Scoped HTTP writes cannot expose hidden media or modify another author's card
Scoped source undo works after the upload grant is released
Independent concurrent writes both commit; conflicting values are rejected
People growth obeys the archive owner's tier and rolls back over-quota writes
